checks.title: Sex-linked pedigrees and testing a model

mc.prompt: Which relationship contradicts a simple fully penetrant X-linked dominant model with an affected father?
mc.answer: An unaffected daughter under the stated ordinary transmission assumptions
mc.explanation: Every daughter should inherit the affected paternal X under the model.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: An unaffected daughter under the stated ordinary transmission assumptions
An unaffected son with an unaffected mother

mc.prompt: An unaffected mother has an affected son in a simple X-linked recessive model with no new mutation. What is inferred?
mc.explanation: She supplied the son’s affected X but has an unaffected phenotype, so a second unaffected allele is present.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: The son inherited the allele on his father’s Y
Every daughter must also be affected
She must have no X chromosome

writing.prompt: Explain why a pedigree analysis should use chromosome transmission as well as the number of affected males and females.
writing.model: The transmission route can create required or impossible allele contributions under a model. Unequal sex counts alone can occur by chance in a small family. Checking every parent–offspring relationship provides stronger evidence than relying on one superficial pattern.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.
Explains the causal relationship or calculation, not just the final result.
Uses the stated evidence and avoids a stronger conclusion than it supports.

writing.prompt: Compare daughters of an affected father and homozygous unaffected mother in X-linked dominant and X-linked recessive models.
writing.model: Every daughter receives the affected paternal X. In a dominant model they express the trait. In a recessive model they also receive an unaffected maternal X and are typically unaffected carriers under the simple assumptions. The chromosome route is the same, but expression differs.

videos.title: Sex-linked pedigrees and testing a model — video support
videos.purpose: Use chromosome transmission to evaluate X-linked models and distinguish consistency from proof in small pedigrees.
videos.fallback: An affected father in an X-linked dominant model passes the affected X to every daughter. With an unaffected mother, sons receive the father's Y and the mother's unaffected X, so they are unaffected under that model. For X-linked recessive inheritance, an affected father with a homozygous unaffected mother has carrier daughters and unaffected sons. The same chromosome route produces a different expressed pattern because the heterozygote phenotype differs. More affected males can be a clue to an X-linked recessive model, but sex counts alone are not decisive. A small autosomal family can also show an uneven distribution by chance.
